spoken_summary.summary_zh:
刷手机不思考就是典型的“脑腐”，大脑处于待机状态。
社交媒体让“脑腐”现象越来越普遍，大家开始担心它对大脑不好。
好消息是：脑腐有办法摆脱，关键是你得主动采取行动。
每天练习大脑，比如开始写作，就能有效预防脑腐。
社交媒体正在改变我们存储信息的方式，意识到危害是第一步。
平衡才是关键，平衡用脑才能成为更好的自己。
spoken_summary.summary_en:
Brain rot means your brain is on autopilot, just scrolling without thinking.
It's becoming more common on social media, and people worry it's bad for the brain.
The good news: there's always a way out, and it starts with taking action.
You can train your brain daily—writing is one simple way to prevent brain rot.
Social media is changing how we store information; awareness of its risks matters.
Balance is key—use your brain wisely to become a better person.
script_zh: 你有没有过这种体验：刷了半天手机，脑子却一片空白？这就是现在网上常说的“脑腐”。它不是说你的脑子坏了，而是说你的大脑根本没在思考，只是在被动地接收信息。
脑腐这个词在社交媒体上越来越火，大家都开始担心：老这么刷下去，脑子会不会真的变笨？这种担心不是没道理，因为社交媒体确实在悄悄改变我们处理信息的方式。
但好消息是，脑腐不是绝症。你完全有办法摆脱它，关键就两个字：行动。你得主动做点什么，而不是任由大脑待机。
最简单的办法，就是每天练习你的大脑。比如开始写作，哪怕只写几句话，也能让大脑重新运转起来。能预防脑腐的事情其实很多，写作只是其中之一。
当然，我们不是要彻底戒掉社交媒体，那不现实。重要的是你得意识到：在上面花太多时间，大概率不是什么好事。有了这个意识，你就能找到平衡。
平衡才是关键。只有平衡用脑，我们才能最好地锻炼大脑，成为更好的自己。所以下次你拿起手机之前，不妨先问自己一句：我现在是在用脑，还是在脑腐？
script_en: Have you ever scrolled for ages and felt like your brain just went blank? That's what people call brain rot. It doesn't mean your brain is broken—it means it's not actually thinking, just passively taking in information.

Brain rot is becoming a hot topic on social media, and people are worried it's really bad for the brain. And that worry makes sense, because social media is quietly changing the way we process information.
But here's the good news: brain rot is not a dead end. There's always a way out, and it starts with one thing—taking action. You have to do something active instead of letting your brain idle.
The simplest fix is to exercise your brain every day. Start writing, even just a few lines—it gets your brain working again. Writing is just one of many things you can do to prevent brain rot.

Of course, we're not saying you should quit social media entirely—that's not realistic. What matters is being aware that too much time on it is probably not a good thing. Once you realize that, you can find balance.
Balance is the key. Only with a balanced brain can we best exercise our mind and become a better person. So next time you pick up your phone, ask yourself: am I using my brain, or is it rotting?

deconstruction.overview: 这是一段典型的短视频口播文案，结构非常清晰：先抛出一个扎心现象（刷手机不思考），再解释概念（脑腐），接着给出解决方案（行动、写作），最后升华到平衡用脑。整体风格口语化、节奏快，用“问题—原因—方案—升华”的经典框架，让观众在几十秒内完成认知刷新并记住一个行动点。

sections.title: 现象引入：你正在脑腐
sections.argument: 你此刻刷手机的行为就是脑腐的典型例子。
sections.evidence: 直接指出观众当下的状态：“What you're doing right now is one clear example of brain rot.”
sections.technique: 第二人称直指（you），制造代入感和冲击力。

sections.title: 定义脑腐：大脑不运转
sections.argument: 脑腐意味着大脑没有在思考，只是被动接收信息。
sections.evidence: 解释为“your brain is not functioning. You're purely looking at things that we're not actually thinking.”
sections.technique: 用简单直白的定义拆解概念，让观众秒懂。

sections.title: 趋势与担忧：越来越普遍
sections.argument: 脑腐在社交媒体上越来越流行，人们相信它对大脑有害。
sections.evidence: “it is getting more popular among social media and people believe this action itself is really bad for your brain.”
sections.technique: 诉诸群体共识（people believe），增强说服力。

sections.title: 转折：有办法摆脱
sections.argument: 脑腐不是无解的，总有办法停止大脑的待机状态。
sections.evidence: “there's always a way to get rid of it. There's always a way to stop your brain from doing that.”
sections.technique: 重复句式（There's always a way）制造节奏感和信心。

sections.title: 解决方案：行动与练习
sections.argument: 摆脱脑腐的关键是采取行动，每天练习大脑，比如写作。
sections.evidence: “take actions... practice your brain. You can start writing.”
sections.technique: 给出具体可操作的动作（写作），让建议落地。

sections.title: 深层影响：社交媒体改变信息存储
sections.argument: 社交媒体正在从根本上改变我们存储信息的方式。
sections.evidence: “social media is just fundamentally changing the way we were saving information.”
sections.technique: 用“fundamentally”强调严重性，提升论点深度。

sections.title: 结论：平衡是关键
sections.argument: 意识到危害并找到平衡，才能最好地锻炼大脑、成为更好的人。
sections.evidence: “Balance is the key for us to best exercise our brain and become a better person.”
sections.technique: 首尾呼应，用“balance”一词收束全文，升华主题。

writing_techniques.name: 第二人称直指
writing_techniques.example: What you're doing right now is one clear example of brain rot.
writing_techniques.effect: 让观众立刻对号入座，产生“说的就是我”的紧迫感。

writing_techniques.name: 重复句式强化节奏
writing_techniques.example: There's always a way to get rid of it. There's always a way to stop your brain from doing that.
writing_techniques.effect: 通过重复传递信心，同时形成口播的韵律感，便于记忆。

writing_techniques.name: 问题—方案—升华结构
writing_techniques.example: 先指出脑腐现象，再给出行动和写作的方案，最后落到平衡用脑。
writing_techniques.effect: 符合短视频观众的认知路径，短时间内完成从焦虑到行动的引导。

writing_techniques.name: 概念拆解通俗化
writing_techniques.example: It means that your brain is not functioning. You're purely looking at things that we're not actually thinking.
writing_techniques.effect: 把抽象概念翻译成日常体验，降低理解门槛。

writing_techniques.name: 关键词收束
writing_techniques.example: Balance is the key for us to best exercise our brain and become a better person.
writing_techniques.effect: 用一个词（balance）总结全文，让观众带走一个核心记忆点。

actionable_skills.skill: 每日大脑练习：自由写作 5 分钟
actionable_skills.how_to_apply: 每天固定一个时间，拿出纸笔或打开文档，连续写 5 分钟，不修改、不评判，想到什么写什么。
actionable_skills.example: 早上起床后，写三句话：昨天最触动我的一件事、今天最重要的一件事、我现在的一个想法。

actionable_skills.skill: 刷手机前先问自己一个问题
actionable_skills.how_to_apply: 每次拿起手机解锁前，停顿 3 秒，问自己：“我现在是在用脑，还是在脑腐？”如果只是无意识消遣，就设定一个 10 分钟闹钟。
actionable_skills.example: 打开短视频 App 前，先默念“我是有目的地看，还是随便刷刷”，然后决定是否打开。

actionable_skills.skill: 设置社交媒体使用边界
actionable_skills.how_to_apply: 给社交媒体 App 设置每日使用时长上限，并把手机放在另一个房间充电，减少无意识拿起手机的次数。
actionable_skills.example: 在手机设置里把 Instagram 每日限额设为 30 分钟，超时后自动锁定。

actionable_skills.how_to_apply: 每看完一条有信息量的内容，用自己的话写一句总结或评论，把被动接收变成主动加工。
actionable_skills.example: 看完一个科普视频后，在备忘录里写：“这个视频讲了 X，我的看法是 Y。”

thinking_models.explanation: 把大脑活动分为主动思考（写作、解决问题）和被动接收（刷视频、无意识滑动），脑腐就是被动模式过载。
thinking_models.how_to_use: 每天结束时回顾：今天主动用脑的时间有多少？被动接收的时间有多少？据此调整第二天的安排。

thinking_models.explanation: 不是彻底戒断，而是找到使用社交媒体的平衡点，让工具服务于人而不是控制人。
thinking_models.how_to_use: 当你想戒掉某个习惯时，先别追求“零”，而是设定一个合理的“度”，比如每天 30 分钟，并定期检查是否超标。

thinking_models.explanation: 改变行为的第一步是建立意识——先意识到问题存在，改变才有可能发生。
thinking_models.how_to_use: 在改掉坏习惯前，先做一周的“觉察记录”，只记录不改变，看看自己什么时候、为什么会出现这个行为。

thinking_models.explanation: 面对负面状态，不要停留在焦虑里，而是立刻采取一个小行动来打破僵局。
thinking_models.how_to_use: 当你感到脑子发木时，不要继续刷手机，而是立刻做一件需要动脑的小事，比如写三句话、算一道题、复述刚看的内容。

golden_sentences.sentence: What you're doing right now is one clear example of brain rot.
golden_sentences.why_good: 第二人称直指，瞬间抓住注意力，让观众无法置身事外。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 你现在正在做的事，就是脑腐的一个典型例子。

golden_sentences.sentence: It means that your brain is not functioning. You're purely looking at things that we're not actually thinking.
golden_sentences.why_good: 用两个短句把抽象概念拆成具体画面，通俗易懂。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 它意味着你的大脑没有在运转。你只是在看东西，并没有真正思考。

golden_sentences.sentence: There's always a way to get rid of it. There's always a way to stop your brain from doing that.
golden_sentences.why_good: 重复句式形成排比，传递信心和节奏感。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 总有办法摆脱它。总有办法阻止你的大脑这样做。

golden_sentences.sentence: Make sure that every day that you understand you can practice your brain.
golden_sentences.why_good: 把“练习大脑”日常化，用 every day 强调持续性。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 确保你每天都明白，你可以锻炼你的大脑。

golden_sentences.sentence: Social media is just fundamentally changing the way we were saving information.
golden_sentences.why_good: 用 fundamentally 一词点出问题的严重性，提升论点分量。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 社交媒体正在从根本上改变我们存储信息的方式。

golden_sentences.sentence: It's important for ours to establish the awareness that too much time on social media probably not a good thing.
golden_sentences.why_good: 用 establish the awareness 强调“意识”的重要性，表达有力。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 对我们来说，建立这样的意识很重要：在社交媒体上花太多时间可能不是好事。

golden_sentences.sentence: As long as you understand that, I think there's a way to get a balance.
golden_sentences.why_good: 条件句 + 信心表达，给出希望和路径。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 只要你明白这一点，我认为就有办法达到平衡。

golden_sentences.sentence: Balance is the key for us to best exercise our brain and become a better person.
golden_sentences.why_good: 用“Balance is the key”收束全文，简洁有力，升华主题。
golden_sentences.chinese_meaning: 平衡是我们最好地锻炼大脑、成为更好的人的关键。

vocabulary.context_sentence: What you're doing right now is one clear example of brain rot.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 脑腐，指因过度消费无脑内容导致思维迟钝；网络流行语，日常聊天可用。

vocabulary.context_sentence: It means that your brain is not functioning.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 运转、发挥功能；常用来描述大脑、机器或系统的运作状态。

vocabulary.context_sentence: You're purely looking at things that we're not actually thinking.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 纯粹地、仅仅；用来强调没有其他成分，口语中很常用。

vocabulary.context_sentence: There's always a way to get rid of it.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 摆脱、去除；日常高频短语，可用于摆脱习惯、物品、情绪等。

vocabulary.context_sentence: Social media is just fundamentally changing the way we were saving information.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 根本上地、彻底地；用于强调变化的深度和本质。

vocabulary.context_sentence: It's important for ours to establish the awareness that too much time on social media probably not a good thing.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 建立意识；正式表达，适合写作或演讲中强调认知转变。

vocabulary.context_sentence: I think there's a way to get a balance.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 达到平衡；口语中常与 work-life balance 等搭配。

vocabulary.context_sentence: Balance is the key for us to best exercise our brain and become a better person.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 锻炼大脑；exercise 此处作动词，表示“锻炼、运用”。

vocabulary.context_sentence: Make sure that every day that you understand you can practice your brain.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 练习大脑；非正式搭配，强调通过重复训练提升脑力。

vocabulary.context_sentence: So the way you're going to do that is take actions.
vocabulary.chinese_note: 采取行动；常用短语，注意通常用 take action（不可数）更标准。
